purpose: Make the annual rural production/work assumptions concrete enough to assess AD200 plausibility while retaining explicit urban-density alternatives.
inputs: Existing candidate supply results/diagnostics, pinned production/work recipe and already inspected Columella task/calendar evidence only. No new source family, simulation or fit in this step.
deliverable: A single annual agricultural budget table tracing rural people to workers, listed hours, crop area/work coefficients, constrained production, rural retention, marketed surplus and delivered town ration equivalents. Identify which quantities are source-supported prescriptions, scenario assumptions or development fits. Quantify existing work-limited production and implied listed hours per rural person; keep omitted processing, draft services, land use, diet and seasonal requirements explicit.
controls: Use each density's own rural pool and all exact existing scenario values. Distinguish physical production from marketed grain and ration-equivalent coverage from resident allocation. Do not equate production forgone under an allowance with recoverable historical output.
decision: Name the largest unresolved agricultural definition and one finite source or implementation change that can constrain it. Prepare high-impact seasonal work only after the annual baseline has explicit compatible units and shared resource definitions.
exclusions: No warehouse/handling-rate detour, modern operational evidence, new parameter sweep, census-density adoption, reserved Buringh/workbook access, climate development or atlas/default change.
